name: NutriCore Protein Lab Kitchen Uniform Set
description: NutriCore operates the protein synthesis kitchens that supply the majority of Tier 1-2 meal services in GLMZ — large industrial facilities that are part laboratory, part production floor, and nothing like a restaurant. The kitchen uniform set issued to production workers reflects this: a white coverall-apron hybrid in a heavy antimicrobial poly-weave that resists the enzymatic cleaners used between production runs, paired with a structured head cover that accommodates horns up to 28cm, pointed ears, bioluminescent crests, and standard hair without separate fittings. The head cover uses a flexible silicone frame rather than fabric elastic, which NutriCore's safety documentation credits with reducing contamination incidents. The apron-front is removable for autoclave cleaning without removing the full coverall. Wrist seals accommodate chrome forearm augmentations and standard limbs identically via a ratchet-adjust band.
cultural_context: NutriCore production work is considered unglamorous but stable — the facilities run twenty-two hours a day and the Collective has negotiated minimum shift guarantees. The uniform is recognizable city-wide; workers often commute in it because changing facilities are inadequate. In Tier 1, a NutriCore uniform means steady work and is treated with a certain respect. The white fabric stains in characteristic ways that experienced workers can read like a history of the facility's output.
story_hooks: A NutriCore production worker notices that one of the enzymatic cleaner runs leaves a residue the standard uniform test strips don't flag — but the residue is accumulating in the wrist seal bands of everyone on their line.

The antimicrobial weave in a specific NutriCore uniform lot has begun to fail at the molecular level after six weeks of use rather than the rated sixteen, and someone in NutriCore's supply chain made a very specific substitution to save money.
A union organizer who disappeared three months ago was last seen in their NutriCore uniform, clocking out of a facility that has no record of them clocking in that day.

physical_description.visual_profile: A stark white coverall-apron system that reads as clinical and industrial — full-body coverage with a structured silhouette that suggests function over form. The white creates an almost sterile presence, interrupted only by dark utility seals at wrists and neck. Worn with a distinctive sculpted head cover that rises above the skull, accommodating augmented anatomy. Overall impression: laboratory technician meets food production worker, wholly utilitarian.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the torso to allow movement and layering over augmentations; tapered slightly at ankles and wrists with compression-style seals. The removable apron-front sits snug against the body, creating a defined waistline when attached. Head cover is form-fitted to the upper skull with generous internal volume.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavy-duty antimicrobial poly-weave in food-grade white — resistant to enzymatic breakdown and caustic cleaners. Silicone-reinforced frame on head cover.
physical_description.texture: Smooth and slightly waxy to the touch, designed to shed moisture and enzymatic residue. Seams are thickly topstitched and visible. The apron-front has a subtle diamond quilting pattern for chemical absorption control.
physical_description.color_scheme: Pristine white as primary; charcoal-gray ratchet seals at wrists and neckline; faint bioluminescent accent piping along seams that activates under facility lighting (brand identifier).
physical_description.closures: Magnetic snaps securing apron-front to coverall body; ratchet-adjust silicone bands at both wrists that accommodate chrome augmentations and organic limbs with equal precision. Head cover secured via a friction-fit silicone base that doesn't require fastening.
distinctive_features: Removable apron-front designed for autoclave sterilization independent of full coverall
Sculpted head cover with asymmetrical crown to accommodate horns up to 28cm and pointed ears without bunching
Ratchet-adjust wrist seals engineered for chrome forearm augmentations
Bioluminescent piping that glows under facility UV (NutriCore branding)
Characteristic stain patterns from protein synthesis output — yellowing at forearms, faint purple-brown spotting on apron from enzymatic residue
Internal data-weave label with worker ID, size, and decontamination cycle count
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 functional corporate uniform — signals stable employment and access to industrial labor infrastructure.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by the 47,000+ NutriCore production workers across GLMZ. Commuter uniform for night-shift workers; badge of steady income in Tier 2 communities. In Tier 1, carries a subtle respect for essential infrastructure work. The staining patterns are readable — dark spotting means protein vat work, purple tints suggest enzymatic algae processing, pristine means admin or new hire.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in; mild yellowing at cuffs and collar from enzymatic exposure. Apron-front typically shows 3-5 characteristic stains that workers wear as evidence of output volume. Creasing at motion points (shoulders, elbows, knees). Silicone seals develop a faint cloudiness after 60+ autoclave cycles.
